headline: Stocks had their best day since April 8 (S&P +2.35%, Dow +1,104) as last week's AI and semiconductor selloff reversed and oil fell about 4–6% on reports of a preliminary Iran deal. Nvidia was the exception, down 4.3% after its board opened a probe into Jensen Huang's alleged Chinese spy link.

Thursday's record chip rout (Nasdaq 100 −6.4%) partly reversed: chips and the Nasdaq gapped sharply higher and the dollar jumped on a blowout payrolls report (+165k vs ~59k expected), but much of the tech gap faded and defensives were sold, so the S&P only gained 0.3%.

A blue-wave backlash against the AI build-out erased Wednesday's post-midterm rally: semis lost 11.6%, the S&P 500 fell 4.4% (its worst day since April 2025) and the VIX jumped 70% to about 28. Bonds caught a modest bid and the dollar and gold barely moved.
